name: Fountain Square redevelopment
dek: A quieter tower, a wetter plaza, and a decade-old question: what is downtown for?
summary: The proposal now before Plan Commission would rebuild the Fountain Square block with mixed-use housing above rebuilt retail, a re-graded plaza, and a civic water feature restored to the square that named it. Status: In review.

name: 1714 Chicago Avenue
dek: A mid-rise on the old bank parcel, now rising story by story.
summary: Steel is up on the former commercial parcel at Chicago and Church. The building will hold 96 apartments over ground-floor retail, with a through-block walk that opens toward the library lawn.

name: Church Street Plaza
dek: A proposed civic room where the bus pulse and the bookstore already meet.
summary: Still in concept: a privately financed public plaza on the south side of Church Street, tying the transit pulse to the independent retail that already holds the block. No entitlements filed.

name: Maple Avenue Residences
dek: Forty-eight homes approved on a quiet block west of the el.
summary: City Council approved a four-story courtyard building of 48 homes, a third of them income-restricted, on a former surface lot. Construction is expected after winter.

name: Lakefront Pavilion restoration
dek: The 1930s shelter is whole again — paint, roof, and a view that never left.
summary: A two-year restoration of the lakefront pavilion is complete: cedar roof, limestone patching, and the original lake-facing openings returned to daylight. The building reopened for weekend programs in August.

name: Main Street Lofts
dek: Work-live studios proposed above the independent mile.
summary: A conversion of two walk-up commercial buildings into twelve work-live lofts, keeping storefronts intact. Plan Commission has the application; neighbors are watching the alley.
